prose: HOLD. The 12-month target price is EUR 27.3, implying 8.7% upside from the current price of EUR 25.11.

The current price assumes Fibres can move beyond FY2025 comparable EBIT of EUR 472m toward a EUR 619m to EUR 743m mid-cycle range. The evidence is constructive but incomplete. Paso de los Toros reached full nominal capacity in the first half of 2026, following its April 2023 operating licence from Uruguay's Ministerio de Ambiente. Hardwood prices were reported at USD 1,200-1,300 per tonne by August 2026, while Suzano was curtailing 3.5% of nominal capacity in 2026. Energy also has support: it generated EUR 181m of comparable EBIT in 2024 on 11.4TWh, and TVO completed final takeover of Olkiluoto 3 in June 2025.

The main challenge to HOLD is that the recovery could exceed the target's assumptions. Financial Data forecasts EBIT of EUR 1.4 billion in 2027, and Energy's 2024 earnings support most of its assigned value at a mid-teens EBIT multiple. However, EBITDA falls from EUR 2.1 billion in 2026e to EUR 1.9 billion in 2027e. Leuna also remains a ramp-up project rather than a proven earnings asset. The evidence supports recovery, but not a clean growth multiple.

An upgrade would require sustained Fibres comparable EBIT above EUR 600m, continued Uruguay utilisation at 2.1Mt, and confirmation that the Sappi JV will close on its end-2026 timetable. A downgrade would follow if Uruguay operates at design capacity but Fibres EBIT stays below EUR 500m, if Finnish captured power prices compress structurally, or if Leuna remains loss-making beyond the guided 2027 sign-change window.

deepDive: ### Current economics

Restated FY2025 sales were EUR 3.5 billion, or 36.6% of group sales. Restated comparable EBIT was EUR 472m, a margin of about 13.4% and 51% of verified comparable-EBIT rows. Allocated EV is EUR 7.4 billion, or 45.5% of group EV. The allocation combines the asset intensity of the Uruguay mills, Finnish mills and newly consolidated forest assets with comparable EBIT. Confidence is Low-Medium because the segment fact gate is degraded and the January 2026 restatement moved Finnish forests into Fibres. Group reported EBIT of EUR 432m is not the right measure for this segment because Fibres' EUR 472m is a post-restatement comparable figure.
### Why the market values it

The EUR 7.4bn allocation depends on mid-cycle cash conversion from a 5.8Mt pulp system, not trough earnings. Paso de los Toros contributes 2.1Mt and Fray Bentos 1.3Mt, giving UPM 3.4Mt of eucalyptus pulp on a low-cost curve. Three Finnish mills add 2.4Mt, mainly softwood, alongside timber and Finnish forest assets now included in the division. The valuation combines spread economics and asset backing rather than a growth multiple. The current price therefore assumes FY2025 comparable EBIT of EUR 472m is below a normalised run-rate, not a new ceiling.
### Market structure and demand

The relevant market is global chemical market pulp, centred on hardwood and eucalyptus pulp sold into tissue, packaging and residual graphic-paper demand. China represents about 43% of world market-pulp demand. Hardwood accounted for 57% of the wood-pulp market by fibre source in 2025. Short-run demand is relatively inelastic, but prices remain cyclical because new supply and utilisation set the marginal price. Tissue and packaging absorb most incremental hardwood demand, while graphic paper continues to reduce integrated demand in Europe.

- Suzano sold 12.7Mt of pulp in the twelve months to March 2026.
- Suzano lists about 13.45Mt of pulp capacity in 2026, around 19% of a roughly 70Mt chemical market-pulp base.
- Fitch previously estimated Suzano at about 31% of hardwood market pulp.
- Arauco has about 5Mt attributable pulp capacity, including 50% of Montes del Plata.
- UPM's 5.8Mt system represents around 8% of global chemical market pulp capacity.

The cycle was at trough-to-early recovery in 2025. Fibres South still generated a 22% EBIT margin in Q3 2025 despite low-cycle hardwood prices. Fibres North was loss-making because of high wood costs and weak softwood prices. Hardwood prices were reported at USD 1,200-1,300 per tonne by August 2026. Suzano chose to run 3.5% below nominal capacity in 2026 to protect spreads. UPM does not need market-share gains for the valuation to work. It needs to retain its roughly 8% system share and earn a mid-cycle spread on that capacity.
### Competitive position and moat

Suzano leads commercially in scale, plantation depth and delivered cost into China. UPM has a eucalyptus cost advantage over Nordic peers because 3.4Mt of capacity is in Uruguay rather than birch-based Nordic operations. Arauco will increase cost-curve competition when Sucuriu starts, while CMPC is a later 2029 risk. Stora Enso is increasingly focused on fluff and packaging and is not the main BHKP volume setter.

- UPM Fibres: 5.8Mt total pulp capacity; 3.4Mt eucalyptus; Paso de los Toros at 2.1Mt design capacity.
- Suzano: 13.45Mt 2026 capacity; about 19% of the 70Mt market-pulp scale; 3.5% curtailment in 2026.
- Arauco: about 5Mt attributable capacity; Sucuriu 3.5Mt targeted for H2 2027.
- CMPC: 2.5Mt current stated mill system; Natureza 2.5Mt targeted for H2 2029.

The moat is mill cash cost and certified fibre supply, not consumer branding. Uruguay plantations cover 495,000 hectares owned and leased. The 2023 operating licence from Uruguay's Ministerio de Ambiente is the operating gate for Paso de los Toros. Finnish mills sit at the other end of the cost curve, with higher wood costs, more flexible operations and a Versowood partnership intended to secure logs. Fibres South and Fibres North do not diversify pulp-price exposure, but they do diversify the system by cash-cost quartile. A hardwood upcycle benefits South first, while softwood weakness or a wood-cost shock hits North first.
### Unit economics and required scale

The unit is a delivered tonne of pulp. Spread equals realised price less wood, chemicals, energy, freight and conversion costs. Management estimates that a EUR 50 per tonne change in average pulp price changes annual group comparable EBIT by approximately EUR 180m net, if paper prices do not follow, and about EUR 270m gross. At 5.8Mt, a EUR 50 per tonne movement equals roughly EUR 290m of gross revenue swing before integration offsets, consistent with the stated EBIT sensitivity.

Maintenance capex on the completed system is modest relative to the EUR 3.47bn Paso de los Toros investment. The investment cycle is largely sunk. The key requirements are design-rate utilisation and a hardwood price sufficiently above Uruguay cash cost to cover depreciation and a cost of capital on the larger asset base. Paso de los Toros reached full 2.1Mt nominal capacity in the first half of 2026. The issue has shifted from construction to monetisation.
### Economics bridge

Allocated EV is EUR 7.4 billion against FY2025 restated comparable EBIT of EUR 472m, implying 15.7x EV/EBIT on current earnings. A 10x framework requires EUR 743m of mid-cycle EBIT, while a 12x framework requires EUR 619m. The volume base is 5.8Mt, including 3.4Mt of eucalyptus capacity at design. The bridge requires a EUR 147m to EUR 271m increase in comparable EBIT, not capacity expansion or market-share gains.
### Bridge sanity check

Revenue equals volume multiplied by realised price. Profit equals spread multiplied by tonnes, less fixed costs. Valuation equals required EBIT multiplied by a 10-12x pulp-cycle multiple. This range fits the historical EV/EBIT record once trough years are recognised: the normative average of 24.8x is distorted by 2023-2025 trough years, while 2021-2022 were closer to 11-12x. This is an EV claim, so group net debt is not allocated to Fibres.

Moving from EUR 472m to EUR 619m-EUR 743m requires a EUR 147m-EUR 271m EBIT increase. This is about one to one-and-a-half times the stated EUR 50 per tonne sensitivity. Hardwood pricing at USD 1,200-1,300 per tonne and Suzano's curtailment make this possible. However, the enlarged 5.8Mt system has not yet delivered a full audited mid-cycle year. The evidence is management sensitivity and Q3 2025 Fibres South margins, rather than a clean full-year earnings record.
### Gap to required economics

- Required EBIT under a 10x framework: EUR 743m.
- FY2025 restated comparable EBIT: EUR 472m.
- Shortfall to the 10x framework: EUR 271m.
- Required change: EUR 50-75/t higher realised pulp price on net sensitivity.
- Operating conditions: full-year Uruguay design utilisation, lower Finnish wood costs and no new structural North downtime.
- A 12x multiple reduces the EBIT gap to EUR 147m but does not remove cycle dependency.
### Milestones and evidence needed

The next 12-24 month tests are sustained 2.1Mt operation at Paso de los Toros, Fray Bentos maintenance without a South-margin collapse, the Finnish wood-cost trend after the Versowood contract, and a full-year Fibres comparable EBIT above EUR 600m. The three-to-five-year test is whether Arauco Sucuriu and later CMPC Natureza create surplus supply and push hardwood prices toward cash cost. Missing evidence includes a reconciled post-restatement cash-cost curve and a clear split between Finnish forest NAV and mill fibre-security value.

- April 2023: Uruguay's Ministerio de Ambiente granted the operating licence for Paso de los Toros.
- 2024: Paso de los Toros reached full design capacity.
- H1 2026: full 2.1Mt nominal capacity was confirmed.
- H2 2027: Arauco Sucuriu, with 3.5Mt capacity, is targeted to start.
- 2029: CMPC Natureza, also 2.5Mt, is the later supply-risk milestone.

The case is invalidated if Uruguay operates at design rates for a year but Fibres cannot exceed EUR 600m of comparable EBIT because prices remain near cash cost. The division is plausible but demanding. Capacity is built and the valuation assumes no market-share gain, but FY2025 results do not support the required spread.
### Assessment

Fibres is the main re-rating driver. It can support the allocation if mid-cycle prices and cash costs return, but not on FY2025 earnings alone. The completed southern pulp system provides the operating base. Market balance, hardwood prices and Finnish wood costs determine whether it delivers the required earnings bridge.

deepDive: ### Current economics

FY2025 sales were EUR 615m, or 6.4% of group sales. Comparable EBIT was EUR 181m in 2024, on EUR 627m of sales and 11.4TWh of generation, for a 28.9% margin. FY2025 comparable EBIT was not verified in the segment fact gate. Allocated EV is EUR 2.5 billion, or 15.5% of group EV, based on an indirect infrastructure or regulated-peer multiple. Confidence is Low-Medium. Energy is a sibling of Fibres in the Finnish industrial system, but its economics differ: it sells megawatt-hours rather than tonnes of fibre.
### Why the market values it

The EUR 2.5bn allocation depends on a 1,900-1,943MW, roughly 12TWh and 99% fossil-free generation portfolio. Assets include owned hydro generation and TVO/Pohjolan Voima nuclear shareholdings. It is valued as infrastructure, not as a merchant-generation growth business. UPM is Finland's second-largest electricity producer. The allocation requires comparable EBIT near the EUR 171m-EUR 381m range seen in 2020-2024. It does not require a return to the 2022 price spike or a fall toward wind-and-solar capture prices.
### Market structure and demand

Finnish electricity production was 79TWh in 2025, against consumption of 85TWh. Pohjolan Voima produced 16.1TWh, or about 20% of Finnish generation. Fortum's Loviisa nuclear plant generated 7.9TWh, around 10% of output. UPM Energy's roughly 12TWh represents about 15% of the same production base. The valuation requires this share to be retained and to earn normal returns, not share gains. No identified operator has a Suzano-like 30% market share. Pohjolan Voima's 20% is the highest among identified Finnish producers.

Demand is supported by electrification and data centres. Supply is increasingly driven by wind, which represented about one quarter of generation. This raises the value of controllable nuclear baseload and hydro balancing, but also increases low and negative power-price hours. UPM estimates that a EUR 10/MWh movement in the Finnish average price on its unhedged net sales position changes annual comparable EBIT by around EUR 40m.
### Competitive position and economic moat

- UPM Energy: about 12TWh, around 15% of Finnish 2025 output, with 722MW hydro and 1,087MW nuclear share capacity.
- Pohjolan Voima: 16.1TWh in 2025, around 20% of Finnish output, with 82% nuclear in its 2025 supply.
- Fortum Loviisa: 7.9TWh in 2025, around 10% of Finnish output.
- TVO Olkiluoto plant: 23.4TWh in 2025; UPM participates through the PVO/TVO system.

Pohjolan Voima is larger in Finland, but operates as a Mankala cost-price vehicle rather than a conventional merchant-margin business. Fortum is larger at group level, with 42.3TWh of total generation in 2025, and is the listed Nordic hydro-and-nuclear peer. UPM's advantage is its mix of nuclear baseload, flexible hydro and industrial offtake within one optimisation book. It is not a regulated allowed-return franchise. TVO's final takeover of Olkiluoto 3 in June 2025 and potential OL1 and OL2 licence extensions beyond 2038 are the main protections for nuclear output.
### Unit economics and required scale

The unit is a generated megawatt-hour, adjusted for hedges. Twelve TWh at a EUR 40/MWh clean spark-equivalent captured margin produces EUR 480m of gross margin before overheads. This is sufficient after costs to support the EUR 181m EBIT achieved in 2024. The requirement is not more terawatt-hours. It is continued availability of roughly 12TWh through OL3 reliability, normal hydro conditions and extended OL1/OL2 operating life, with captured prices not fully competed away by wind.

Future capital spending is focused on life extension and automation, not a new nuclear reactor. The main risk is structural compression in Finnish captured prices, not volume growth. Nuclear output is shared through the PVO/TVO structure and does not belong exclusively to this division. Hydro and nuclear exposure also does not diversify Fibres from wider Finnish industrial conditions.
### Economics bridge

Allocated EV of EUR 2.5 billion against latest verified comparable EBIT of EUR 181m implies 14.0x EV/EBIT. A 12x framework requires EUR 211m of EBIT, while a 10x framework requires EUR 253m. The EUR 30m to EUR 72m gap is modest against the EUR 40m annual EBIT sensitivity for each EUR 10/MWh change in Finnish average prices. The volume base is roughly 12TWh and 1,900MWe. Price capture, not capacity growth, drives earnings.
### Bridge sanity check

Infrastructure-style earnings can be expressed as available capacity multiplied by captured price, multiplied by one less the operating-cost ratio. Valuation can be expressed as EBIT multiplied by a 10-14x range typical of Nordic hydro and nuclear portfolios. FY2024 EBIT of EUR 181m supports almost all of the EUR 2.5bn allocation at 14x. A 12x or 10x framework requires only EUR 30m-EUR 72m more EBIT, less than two times the stated EUR 10/MWh sensitivity.

Feasibility is high if Finnish prices do not collapse structurally. Evidence on unit economics is better than for Fibres because generation, sensitivity and the 2020-2024 EBIT series are disclosed. It is weaker on current-year EBIT and the internal fair-value mark for Energy shareholdings. The bridge works at 14x and remains plausible, but demanding, at 10x.
### Gap to required economics

- Required EBIT at 12x: EUR 211m.
- Latest verified comparable EBIT: EUR 181m in 2024.
- Shortfall to the 12x framework: EUR 30m.
- Price needed to close the gap: EUR 8-10/MWh higher captured price on the unhedged book.
- Operating conditions: normal hydrology and OL3 availability in line with 2025-2026 operations.
- Alternative valuation support: the 14x allocation closes the gap with almost no EBIT growth.
### Milestones and evidence needed

The next 12-24 month requirements are disclosure of FY2025 and FY2026 comparable EBIT, the hedge ratio and UPM's fair-value mark for its Energy shareholdings. The three-to-five-year gate is an OL1/OL2 operating licence extension beyond 2038. TVO's final takeover of Olkiluoto 3 in June 2025 was the latest commercialisation milestone, and the unit is in its second full year of commercial production. The case fails if Finnish captured prices fall structurally, leaving Energy EBIT near the low EUR 100m range despite high nuclear availability.
### Assessment

Energy is supported by current economics if the multiple remains in the mid-teens. The fragile assumptions are the multiple and future Finnish price capture, not megawatt-hour availability. It is the strongest current-earnings offset to the Fibres cycle in the group EV allocation.

deepDive: ### Current economics

UPM Adhesive Materials generated nearly EUR 1.6bn of sales in 2024. LinkedIn commentary from the business points to nearly EUR 1.7bn in 2025, but this is not in Financial Data and is treated as a company-source lead rather than a control total. Allocated EV is EUR 2.2 billion, or 13.6% of group EV. FY2025 EBIT was not verified in the fact gate. Q3 2025 comparable EBIT was EUR 33m, equivalent to an 8% margin on sales.
### Why the market values it

The EUR 2.2bn allocation is based on growth and mix from a global number-two label-materials franchise. The business is expanding into graphics through Metamark, Grafityp and AMC, and into advanced labels in the United States, Malaysia and Vietnam, while closing Nancy. Avery Dennison remains the market leader in self-adhesive materials, while UPM is the named European and global number two. The valuation requires growth and margin recovery after bolt-on integration, not a pulp-cycle multiple.
### Market structure and competitive position

The review does not establish a precise 2025 volume share of the global self-adhesive label market. The self-adhesive labels market is cited at about USD 64bn in 2025, but this is a broad revenue pool rather than UPM's directly addressable laminate-materials market. Applying EUR 1.6bn of 2024 sales to this figure implies only a low-single-digit share. It does not imply dominance or a market-share requirement in the valuation. The commercial challenge is to retain differentiated label-materials mix against Avery Dennison, not to lead the whole label market.
### Unit economics and required scale

Unit economics are contribution per square metre of laminate. Key drivers are coating utilisation, adhesive formulation, liner and face-stock input costs, and mix in wine, pharmaceutical and industrial labels. Capital intensity is much lower than in Fibres. Adhesive Materials shares label and packaging converter customers with Specialty Papers, but sells pressure-sensitive laminate and graphics materials rather than paper reels. Strong label demand can support both businesses rather than requiring one to displace the other.
### Economics bridge and assessment

The 2024 EBITDA growth rate of 12% shows that the platform can scale. However, the 8% Q3 2025 comparable EBIT margin indicates that mix, efficiency and integration work remain incomplete. The allocation requires mid-cycle EBIT margins in the high-single-digit to low-double-digit range, on a sales base that continues to outgrow GDP after acquisitions are absorbed. The division is plausible but demanding. Missing evidence includes verified FY2025 EBIT and a clear split between organic and M&A-driven growth.

deepDive: ### Current economics

Biofuels and Biochemicals is included in Other Operations. Restated comparable EBIT for Other Operations was negative EUR 180m in FY2025. Lappeenranta biofuels, with around 130,000 tonnes of advanced renewable-fuel capacity, returned to a positive EBIT contribution by late 2025. Leuna has 220,000 tonnes of wood-based chemicals capacity and a revised EUR 1.2 billion investment estimate. It made first customer deliveries of industrial sugars in Q4 2025. Allocated EV is EUR 1.2 billion, or 7.3% of group EV, on an option-value basis. Confidence is Low.
### Why the market values it

The EUR 1.2bn allocation depends on future delivery, not current revenue. Leuna must generate sufficient volume, price and margin to justify approximately the committed capex. Management guides to full production and positive EBIT during 2027. The platform follows Fibres' wood and residual-stream logic, but it is a different business. Fibres sells a cyclical commodity tonne, while this segment sells drop-in chemicals and fuels through offtake contracts with a regulatory overlay.

A Fibres volume shock would not automatically stop Leuna. However, failure of the industrial case for wood-based drop-ins would strand both the biochemicals option and part of the broader beyond-pulp strategy. The allocation is not based on current earnings. It is an option valued at approximately the Leuna capex already committed.
### Market structure and required share capture

The relevant chemicals market is renewable bio-MEG and adjacent glycols and lignin fillers, not the full fossil MEG market. The renewable bio-MEG market has been estimated at about USD 568m in 2025. India Glycols is an established commercial bio-MEG producer, while Braskem and other bio-ethylene participants use different feedstock routes. The broader fossil MEG market is around 38Mt. Leuna is immaterial at commodity scale but could matter in a small renewable niche.

If Leuna's glycol output is around 100,000 tonnes against a renewable MEG market of only a few hundred thousand tonnes, the valuation implies a double-digit percentage share of the renewable niche by 2027-2028. This would be ambitious in a small specialist market and far above India Glycols' historic specialist position. It would still be a rounding error in the fossil MEG market. The required share is therefore ambitious in renewable MEG and irrelevant in bulk MEG.
### Unit economics and economics bridge

The investment must earn specialty-chemical margins rather than bulk-glycol economics. A 10x EBIT framework on EUR 1.2 billion requires approximately EUR 119m of EBIT. Applied to Leuna's 220,000 tonnes, this equals roughly EUR 540 per tonne of EBIT. This requires yields, pricing, product mix and customer offtake that generate specialty value from industrial sugars, bio-MEG, functional fillers and related wood-based chemical products.

The fuels business is smaller and more narrowly positioned. Lappeenranta's 130,000-tonne renewable-fuels base does not compete at the same scale as Neste, which sold around 870,000 tonnes of sustainable aviation fuel in 2025 and targets 6.8Mt of renewable-fuel capacity by 2027. UPM's upside is low-capex debottlenecking and aviation offtake if CTO-derived SAF receives ASTM and CORSIA qualification, not a scaled refinery race.
### Signal map

- April 2023: Uruguay granted Paso de los Toros a full operating licence; this is a shared wood-system gate with Fibres rather than a chemicals approval.
- 12 December 2023: UPM increased Leuna's investment estimate to EUR 1.18bn and expected startup at end-2024.
- 24 May 2024 and 27 May 2025: UPM suspended and then discontinued Rotterdam biofuels-refinery planning.
- 19 December 2025: Landesverwaltungsamt Sachsen-Anhalt permitted industrial-scale Leuna production and commercialisation within the 220,000-tonne envelope.
- Q4 2025: Leuna made first industrial-sugar deliveries to customers.
- February 2026: a US SFI and EPA pathway supported bio-products exported to the United States.
- H1 2026: commercial wood-based chemicals from Leuna were reported in the market.

Progress is mixed but measurable. The chemicals business has moved from construction to permitted industrial production and first volumes. The fuels business has been reduced because Rotterdam was cancelled and Lappeenranta is being debottlenecked rather than replicated. The next gate is ASTM and CORSIA acceptance for CTO-derived SAF, expected around 2027 Q1. Approval would support aviation offtake and a low-capex Lappeenranta expansion. Rejection would leave the fuels business more reliant on road-transport mandates.
### Regulatory and competitive challenges

The negative signals are material. Rotterdam's cancellation removed the scaled fuels-growth case. RED III fragmentation limits uniform advanced-fuel marketing across the European Union. As of 15 March 2026, only a subset of member states, including the Netherlands, Denmark and Italy, had fully transposed the framework cited in the review. This weakens the case for treating European regulation as one secure demand pool.

- Renewable bio-MEG market: about USD 568m in 2025.
- Fossil MEG market: around 38Mt, where Leuna remains immaterial.
- Lappeenranta advanced renewable fuels: about 130,000 tonnes.
- Neste SAF sales: about 870,000 tonnes in 2025.
- Neste renewable-fuel capacity target: 6.8Mt by 2027.
- Management target: Leuna full production and positive EBIT during 2027.
### Gap to required economics

The platform starts from a negative EUR 180m comparable EBIT contribution within Other Operations. Nearly all of the EUR 1.2 billion allocation therefore depends on future performance. Positive EBIT in 2027 is a management target, not a demonstrated run-rate. The key challenge is not just reaching capacity. Leuna must sustain yield, high-value product mix, contracted offtake and specialty margins of roughly EUR 540 per tonne of capacity on the 10x EBIT framework.
### Milestones and evidence needed

The next evidence points are Leuna utilisation, customer offtake, product mix and EBIT direction through 2026 and 2027. The German operating permit reduces chemicals regulatory risk, but does not validate commercial yields or pricing. For fuels, the ASTM and CORSIA decision is the key binary gate. A positive Lappeenranta contribution late in 2025 is constructive, but does not offset Rotterdam's cancellation or establish a large fuels platform.
### Assessment

The EUR 1.2bn allocation is speculative. Capex has been committed and the project has progressed from construction to first deliveries, but the 2027 EBIT sign change remains the main proof point. The platform can create value if Leuna achieves specialty-chemical economics. It can also consume cash longer than expected if utilisation, yield or offtake disappoint.

Pretax profit of EUR 690m and net earnings of EUR 491m reconcile across sources. The difference reflects comparability items, including restructuring, mill closures, forest fair-value movements and classification effects. Comparable EBIT is therefore the more relevant recurring operating measure for allocation than Financial Data's EUR 432m EBIT.

Communication Papers likely has a much larger sales share than its 6.7% EV share, consistent with its 4.6x LTM EBITDA JV multiple. Biofuels and Biochemicals contributes little current profit but receives 7.3% of EV, roughly matching the revised EUR 1.18bn Leuna investment.
coreAnalysis.analyticalAnchor: The allocation is credible only if Fibres earns a mid-cycle pulp spread on its 5.8Mt system, Energy continues to monetise roughly 12TWh of fossil-free generation, and Leuna stops consuming cash by 2027. Fibres is decisive because a EUR 50/t pulp movement changes group comparable EBIT by EUR 180m-EUR 270m.

groupedPools.heading: ### UPM Specialty Papers: resilient packaging and labelling paper engine
paragraphs: Specialty Papers has allocated EV of EUR 1.5 billion, or 9.1% of group EV, against FY2025 sales of approximately EUR 1.3 billion. It is valued using a fallback EBITDA or EBIT multiple on its revenue base because the fact gate does not provide a verified comparable EBIT figure.

The key issue is whether its packaging and labelling paper mix can remain distinct from structurally declining graphic paper. Value depends on packaging and label demand growth, durable margins and the ability to sustain a higher-quality earnings profile than Communication Papers.

groupedPools.heading: ### UPM Communication Papers: transaction-defined exit value
paragraphs: Communication Papers is valued at EUR 1.1 billion, or 6.7% of EV, based on the definitive Sappi JV agreement signed on 28 May 2026. The EUR 1.1bn EV is about 4.6x LTM EBITDA to September 2025, providing a direct anchor for the allocation.

At closing, UPM is due EUR 475m cash, an EUR 88m preferential shareholder-loan receivable, an EUR 10m additional shareholder-loan receivable and 50% JV equity with EUR 167m book value. EUR 411m of net pension and other liabilities would transfer to the JV. Closing remains subject to Sappi shareholder approval and EU and other antitrust clearances, with an end-2026 target.

groupedPools.heading: ### UPM Plywood: WISA Group standalone valuation
paragraphs: Plywood is allocated EUR 380m, or 2.3% of EV, based on an estimated peer wood-products multiple of about 6.9x FY2025 comparable EBITDA of EUR 55m. FY2025 sales were EUR 409m. This is an estimate, not a market-clearing transaction price.

The Board approved a demerger plan on 29 April 2026 to separate UPM Plywood into WISA Group Plc. Shareholders are expected to receive one WISA share per UPM share. The EGM is expected in early September 2026. Completion is planned for 31 October 2026, with a Nasdaq Helsinki listing expected around 2 November 2026. Debt allocation remains undisclosed.

crossPoolBridge: Financial Data forecasts sales of EUR 9.9 billion in 2026 and EUR 10.2 billion in 2027, versus EUR 9.7 billion in 2025. EBITDA rises from EUR 1 billion in 2025 to EUR 2.1 billion in 2026, before easing to EUR 1.9 billion in 2027. EBIT rises from EUR 432m in 2025 to EUR 1.1 billion in 2026 and EUR 1.4 billion in 2027.

The 2026-2027 forecast reflects a cycle and mix recovery, not a new business immediately appearing in the income statement. The EBIT increase from EUR 432m to EUR 1.1 billion exceeds Fibres' entire FY2025 comparable EBIT. It requires pulp spreads to normalise, hydro and nuclear output to be normal, less capital destruction in Communication Papers, and lower Leuna start-up costs.

Consensus EBIT of EUR 1.1 billion in 2026 matches Financial Data. However, consensus EBITDA of EUR 1.7 billion is below Financial Data's EUR 2.1 billion. This gap is the weakest part of the group bridge, making EBIT the more useful common forecast metric when the two data sets diverge.

Existing businesses can support much of 2026e EBIT if Fibres and Energy deliver. Leuna optionality and the Sappi JV and WISA restructuring change the group's shape more than 2026 cash generation. FCFF falls to EUR 687m in 2027 as gross capex rises to EUR 920m, showing that the investment cycle is not fully complete in the forecast.
coreAnalysis.bridgeMechanics: Reported FY2025 EBIT of EUR 432m is not the run-rate. Comparable EBIT of EUR 921m is the cleaner operating baseline. Starting from reported EBIT would overstate the recovery required, while treating comparable EBIT as already mid-cycle would understate remaining pulp leverage.
valuationRealityCheck: At 12x EBIT, Fibres' FY2025 comparable EBIT of EUR 472m supports approximately EUR 5.7 billion of EV, or 76% of its EUR 7.4 billion allocation. The remaining EUR 1.8 billion depends on a pulp-cycle recovery. At 14x EBIT, Energy's EUR 181m FY2024 comparable EBIT supports approximately EUR 2.5 billion, covering its EUR 2.5 billion allocation.

Communication Papers is fully supported by the signed EUR 1.1 billion transaction anchor. Plywood is supported by FY2025 comparable EBITDA of EUR 55m at an estimated 6.9x multiple. Biofuels and Biochemicals is not supported by current EBIT: its EUR 1.2 billion value is an option broadly equal to the Leuna investment.

Applying the 2026e EV/EBIT multiple of 14.5x to FY2025 Financial Data EBIT of EUR 432m supports only about EUR 6.3bn of EV, less than 40% of the EUR 16.3 billion control total. This is the wrong test because FY2025 reported EBIT is trough-like and affected by comparability items. Applying 12x to comparable EBIT of EUR 921m supports about EUR 11.1bn, or 68% of EV.

The remaining third of EV reflects Fibres cycle recovery, Energy's infrastructure multiple, Adhesive Materials growth and Leuna optionality. The EV-to-equity bridge is direct: EUR 16.3 billion EV less EUR 3.1 billion of net debt and other claims equals EUR 13.2 billion market cap. Finnish forest assets remain in Fibres as fibre-security backing and are not treated as separately realisable NAV.

The valuation is defensible if 2026-2027 EBIT reaches approximately EUR 1.1bn-EUR 1.4bn and the Sappi JV closes. It fails if pulp remains near cash cost through 2027, Finnish captured power prices compress structurally, and Leuna remains loss-making beyond the guided 2027 window. The largest uncertainty is the Fibres spread.
scenarios: The bear case uses EUR 1.4 billion of EBITDA and an 8.0x EV/EBITDA multiple, implying EUR 11.2 billion EV. After EUR 3.1 billion of claims, this equals EUR 15.4 per share. It assumes pulp remains near cash cost, Energy captured price falls by EUR 15/MWh, Leuna remains loss-making, and the Sappi JV is delayed.

The base case uses EUR 1.9 billion of 2027e EBITDA and the same 8.0x multiple, implying EUR 15.5 billion EV and EUR 23.5 per share after claims. It assumes the JV closes and Leuna approaches breakeven, but does not require an exceptional pulp cycle.

The bull case uses EUR 2.4 billion EBITDA at 8.0x, implying EUR 19.2 billion EV and EUR 30.5 per share after claims. It requires Fibres EBIT above EUR 700m, a normal Energy year, positive Leuna EBIT and improved Adhesive Materials mix.

The scenarios hold net debt at the EUR 3.1 billion control residual, so earnings changes are not confused with balance-sheet optionality. If the Sappi JV closes, UPM receives EUR 475m cash, EUR 98m of shareholder-loan receivables and 50% JV equity with EUR 167m book value. EUR 411m of net pension and other liabilities transfer. The scenario table does not include these changes because closing remains conditional.
coreAnalysis.bottomLine: The central question is whether FY2025 was a trough after completion of the southern pulp system, or the start of a structurally narrower spread. Fibres decides the answer. Energy can support its EUR 2.5bn allocation through disclosed terawatt-hours and a mid-teens EBIT multiple. Adhesive Materials needs margin recovery, Communication Papers and Plywood are exit mathematics, and Leuna is an option roughly equal to committed capex. Key indicators are quarterly Fibres comparable EBIT, Finnish area power prices against Energy's EUR 40m per EUR 10/MWh sensitivity, and the Sappi JV antitrust timetable.

scenarioValuation.keyConditions: The scenarios depend mainly on the Fibres pulp spread, Uruguay utilisation, Finnish power-price capture and Leuna's path to positive EBIT. Each uses the same 8.0x EV/EBITDA multiple, so valuation differences reflect operating delivery rather than multiple expansion. Net debt is held at the EUR 3.1 billion control residual, excluding the potential balance-sheet benefit of Sappi JV closing. These scenarios are operating boundary cases, not probability-weighted target-price inputs. The code-verified 12-month target of EUR 27.3 sits between Base and Bull (Bear EUR 15.4, Base EUR 23.5, Bull EUR 30.5); its method weights are shown in the Target Price Bridge.
scenarioValuation.thesisBreaker: A prolonged pulp surplus that leaves Fibres below EUR 500m EBIT despite full Uruguay utilisation would break the cross-segment valuation case.

catalysts.prose:
Pulp price has the largest equity impact because it can add or remove several hundred million euros of group comparable EBIT without new capacity. Paso de los Toros operating consistently at its 2.1Mt design rate would show whether price and spread are sustainable rather than ramp-up effects. Lower Finnish wood costs would improve the weaker northern system.

The Sappi process is the clearest binary catalyst, with an end-2026 target, defined cash consideration and a measurable regulatory path. Leuna should be assessed on utilisation, product mix and EBIT, not first-delivery announcements. First industrial-sugar deliveries mark commercial commencement, not the positive EBIT outcome required in 2027.

risks.prose:
The key risk is a pulp surplus lasting through Arauco Sucuriu's planned start-up, leaving Uruguay at design capacity but Fibres unable to generate more than EUR 500m of EBIT. FY2025 northern earnings partly show this risk. It is not fully reflected if the EUR 7.4bn Fibres allocation assumes a normalised hardwood spread.

Some risks are partly priced: graphic-paper decline is reflected in the 4.6x JV multiple, Rotterdam has been cancelled, and Energy earnings are below the 2022 peak. Less reflected are degraded segment disclosure, unverified FY2025 figures for several divisions and WISA's undisclosed debt allocation. Risks can compound if weak pulp coincides with Leuna cash consumption and delayed portfolio transactions.

### 3. Valuation Method Rationale

EV/EBITDA is the primary method for UPM as a cyclical, asset-heavy industrial; P/E provides an equity-value cross-check on the 2027e earnings recovery. UPM trades at 8.43x 2027e EV/EBITDA versus a 7.8x peer median and 12.93x normalized historical average; these references support an 8.0x–10.0x fair-value band. The selected 9.0x sits at the midpoint of that band: 2027e EBIT margin improves to 13.6% from 11.4% in 2026e, but EBITDA declines to EUR 1.9 billion from EUR 2.1 billion and net debt/EBITDA rises to 1.43x from 1.25x, limiting the premium to peers and retaining a material discount to history. The supporting 14.0x P/E is close to the 13.7x 2027e peer median and well below UPM’s 26.22x normalized historical average. The ROE/P/BV scatter signal receives its prescribed 20% weight because UPM’s asset-heavy profile and 9.5% average forecast ROE make the implied 1.5x P/BV signal relevant; the principal valuation risk is weaker-than-forecast EBITDA and margin delivery, which would shift the fair multiple toward the low end of the selected band.
